discussion_comments.comment_body: This is intentional. The crates.io, PyPI, npm, and WASM packages have independent version histories and publishing workflows. The Python package was already at 0.2.5 while the Rust crate was at 0.1.6 before this PR, so 0.2.6 is the correct next PyPI release. Aligning the ecosystems would require a separate coordinated versioning-policy migration rather than changing this bump.

Good catch on the drift. Fixed in 50dc4e5 by switching pyproject.toml to `dynamic = ["version"]`, so maturin sources the version from `Cargo.toml` `[package] version` and the Python metadata can't diverge from the crate again (it had been stuck at 0.1.0 since the PyO3 bindings landed).

Note this is metadata hygiene rather than a release-path change: no workflow auto-publishes the Python package — `publish-crate.yml` (crates.io) and `publish.yml` (npm) are the only publish jobs, and both are covered by the Cargo.toml / napi bumps in this PR.
